questions.prompt: Map NetTrello's validation layers from browser to aggregate: what does each one catch?

keyPoints.text: Client-side forms stop obviously bad input before a request is even sent.
At the endpoint boundary, the concurrency header is parsed and a malformed value is rejected with a 400.
The shared Guard helper handles the generic string and number rules.
keyPoints.quote: Required strings, max lengths, non-negative numbers

keyPoints.text: The Board aggregate owns relational invariants, like assignees.
Columns enforce their own card-limit invariant at the moment a card is inserted.
The layering has a purpose split: UX up front, system protection in the domain.
keyPoints.quote: Client validation improves UX; domain validation protects the system.

questions.prompt: Describe the current auth boundary. What are 'members' in this system, and what are they not?

keyPoints.text: There is no authn or authz anywhere in the API.
keyPoints.quote: No authentication or authorization code was found.

keyPoints.text: None of the mapped endpoints demand authorization or inspect caller identity.
Members are seed-time display records, nothing more.
keyPoints.quote: Members currently exist as display data in seed storage

keyPoints.text: CORS narrows which browsers may call, but is no security boundary.
keyPoints.quote: non-browser clients can still call endpoints

keyPoints.text: The assignee guard validates data consistency only.
keyPoints.quote: it does not prove the caller can edit the board

keyPoints.text: Permission decisions belong on the server, never inferred from hidden UI.
keyPoints.quote: server endpoints must enforce resource access

questions.prompt: Work the guide's drill: adding board-membership authorization to MoveCardAsync. Where do you anchor, and what has to exist first?

keyPoints.text: The route layer gives you boardId and cardId as anchors for the check.
Every mutation funnels through MutateAsync, the natural single seam to interpose a membership check.
Seeded board members supply the data you would authorize against once callers are identified.
The aggregate already walks the member list for assignees - a template for a caller-membership guard.
Avoid the junior trap of pointing at the existing assignee validation as if it were access control.
